because: Counterexample (hunt 2026-10-10): a cursor file named *.tmp was its own temporary file (with_extension), truncated in place before the new bytes were synced; a write failure left neither the old nor the new cursor. Fix: the temporary file is the cursor's name plus .tmp.
evidence_text: `a_damaged_cursor_rereads_the_log_instead_of_skipping_it` (empty, truncated and non-JSON cursors; mutation "damaged = missing" fails it), `a_cursor_is_replaced_not_rewritten_in_place_whatever_its_name`
statement: The saved cursor is replaced durably (temporary file synced, renamed, directory synced). A cursor file that exists but cannot be read or parsed starts reading the current file from its start, never its end; a missing cursor follows `--from-start`. Re-read alerts are bounded by the forwarding age and deduplicated by event id at the node.
